//: Copy to <your-repo>/.claude/work.config.json and edit. Every key is OPTIONAL — the harness runs single-host, local-only, with no repo identity if this file is absent. Keys marked REQUIRED-FOR are only needed for the feature named.
//repo: REQUIRED-FOR cloud leads and the preflight identity check. These five values used to be hardcoded in work-runner.mjs; that is what made the harness un-shareable.
//repo.mergeMode: How the shepherd lands a PR (DER-2753). "queue" = arm the native GitHub merge queue with `gh pr merge <n> --auto` and let the queue own the strategy. "direct" = the shepherd merges itself with `gh pr merge <n> --<mergeStrategy> --delete-branch` — for the MAJORITY of repos, which have no merge queue. OMIT the key to auto-detect once per `ready` call (GraphQL repository.mergeQueue on the default branch). If the probe cannot answer, the mode stays UNRESOLVED and NOTHING is merged — set it explicitly rather than let the harness guess. In direct mode the harness reproduces client-side the only protection the queue was giving you: it merges ONLY when `ready` passes every gate (not draft, 0 unresolved threads, Codex on head, checks pass, gate evidence current).
//repo.mergeStrategy: direct mode only: "squash" (default) | "merge" | "rebase". Ignored in queue mode, where passing a strategy is a documented mistake.
//repo.allowMergeWithoutChecks: A LOOSENING — default false, leave it false if you have any CI. A public repo with NO required checks reports no check surface at all, so `ready` reads checks=UNKNOWN and, fail-closed, never lets anything merge. Set true to merge on the remaining gates (draft / threads / Codex-on-head / gate evidence) when there is genuinely no CI to wait for. It waives ONLY an ABSENT check surface: a red or pending check still blocks the merge with this on. The waiver is printed in the `ready` verdict and recorded on `run_started`, so it stays auditable.
//trustedCommentAuthors: SECURITY (DER-2737). PR comments are how a CLOUD lead reports lifecycle events (WORK-EVENT / WORK-HANDOFF), and the fold treats them as privileged ledger input — so it accepts them ONLY from these logins, plus `repo.ownerLogin` and known harness bots. Deny-by-default: with no `repo.ownerLogin` configured, NO human login is trusted and comment folding is off. Add a second maintainer or a bot that posts on the harness's behalf here. Anyone who can comment on any open PR in the repo can otherwise write your ledger.
//commitAuthor: Commits are authored as this identity. Some deploy checks (e.g. Vercel) map commit author → account and red the PR on a mismatch.
//hosts: Where leads run. `local` always exists. `kind:"ssh"` overflows to another machine over cmux ssh; `kind:"cloud"` is a Claude Code cloud environment spawned via the RemoteTrigger tool. One entry PER ACCOUNT — environmentId is per-account and credProfile pins which login it is spawned from.
//preferHosts: Default host order for every lead when the run sets no --host/--prefer. pickHost fills-then-spills across them.
//worktreeRoot: Where per-issue worktrees are created. Must be outside the repo.
//collision: How the harness decides two issues cannot run in parallel. versionHolder* name files whose concurrent edits pass git but fail a CI version guard; serializedFiles are files only one in-flight PR may touch; scopeKeySegments is how many path segments make a scope key.
//dockerScopePrefixes: Issues touching these paths need a Docker-capable host (real-database tests). Feeds the pickHost capability gate so such an issue is never spilled to a noDocker host.
//budget: Per-issue circuit breaker. A trip is a decision point (split / re-scope / park), not an auto-kill.
//shepherdModel: The shepherd's inline fixes merge with no second reviewer, so default it to your strongest model.
//leadTypes: OPTIONAL. Non-default lead models. `proxy:true` routes through a local gateway (localhost only); `provider` names a direct third-party endpoint. Tokens are NEVER stored here — the harness builds a runtime shell expression that reads them from your gateway config or repo env file at launch, so no key reaches a ledger event or a logged command line.
//modelPrices: OPTIONAL. USD per 1M tokens, for the cost column in `work-metrics`. Deliberately empty by default — a stale price table silently reports wrong money.
